name: @patternlike/api

scripts.//build: Dry-runs the SAME environment `deploy` ships. Without --env production this validated the top-level dev block (AUTH_STUB=1, issuer.invalid, the placeholder D1 id) and so could never catch a production-only config error; it also tripped Workers Builds' Worker-name check, whose remedy is a PR renaming the top-level worker to patternlike-api-production. Requires apps/web/dist to exist — see the root //build note.
scripts.//typecheck: BOTH configs. Worker sources compile without Node types on purpose; scripts/ needs them. One command so a script cannot drift out of the gate.
scripts.//publisher:model:verify: PRODUCTION GATE, not part of any test lane. Calls the authorized account's model endpoint with OPENAI_API_KEY and proves the pinned model exists. Required before initial enablement and before every later model change.
scripts.//publisher:eval:live: PRODUCTION GATE, not part of any test lane. Sends the checked-in SYNTHETIC corpus to the real provider with OPENAI_API_KEY and scores what comes back through validateReadingCandidate. Reads no D1, no account, and no real birth data. Required before initial enablement and before every later model, prompt, selection-policy, or validation-policy change; the single synthetic canary does not substitute for it. The offline half of the same corpus runs in `npm test`.
scripts.//deploy: Ships apps/web/dist as static assets. Prefer `npm run deploy:api` from the repository root, which builds the web app first.
scripts.//db:local: Applies the ordered db/d1 directory, not just 0001. Deleting .wrangler state is an explicit developer reset, not the migration mechanism.

//moment-timezone: DATA ONLY. src/services/tzdb.ts imports data/packed/latest.json and decodes it; the library's own runtime is a UMD file inside a CommonJS package that @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers refuses to load, and pulling in `moment` to answer two questions would put a date-formatting library in a Worker that needs neither. The dependency exists so package-lock.json pins the tz database version M5 day boundaries are resolved against — Intl exposes none.
